limits: Usefulness evidence is not used for automatic selection or maturity.
All assigned outcomes enter the estimate, not only activations.
Adaptive access value is not lifetime topology value or final ablation effect.
Reused development seeds and a short window do not establish reliable superiority.
Recovery includes ordinary pruning and random replacement births; it does not isolate edge plasticity.

interpretation: Recovery was partial and nonuniform. No probed arm exceeded its always-enabled reference at the final development evaluation.
Seed 2 probed trials improved from 94 to 98, but their final offline masked policies scored 113. That is not an autonomous removal or achieved policy score.

Seed 2 always-enabled trials helped their current policies (101 to 94 when masked), while a separately trained no-addition policy reached 115. Final ablation dependence and the benefit of an addition during training are different quantities.
Ordinary lifecycle turnover occurred: 10 to 14 retirements and 9 to 13 replacement births per arm. All twelve added trials survived. This cannot isolate edge-learning recovery from topology changes.
157 distinct focused tests passed. The completed retry executed 9216 moves; an interrupted attempt separately accounts for at least 6016 more plus unknown in-flight work.

Keep probing experimental. Next isolate edge learning from lifecycle turnover with an experimental fixed-topology recovery control whose weights remain plastic. No handover, reliable M1 mastery or usefulness-driven retention claim follows.
